newsitem.title: USA: Texas Comptroller preps Texas-Mexico border report.
newsitem.headline: Texas Comptroller preps Texas-Mexico border report.

text.p: Texas Comptroller John Sharp's office is expected to issue a "massive" report concerning the Texas-Mexico border late this year or early next, a spokesman for his office said Wednesday.

In early 1994, Sharp issued a three-volume report called "Forces of Change," Kelly Fero, a spokesman for the comptroller said. Two years in the making, the report covered a 30-year period running to 2025, Fero said.
"It identified what (Sharp) believes to be these kind of unavoidable forces of change like an aging population (and) deteriorating infrastructure," Fero said.
The report then presented a plan for Texas to deal with those changes, and place itself in the best possible position handle with them, Fero aid.
"It's basically a blue print for the next generation of Texans," Fero said. The award-winning report is still referred to, and has become part of the state's "public policy landscape," Fero said.

"(Sharp) is now going to do a similar thing, but about the border area," he said, adding that the report will address such topics as education, the environment and the North American Free Trade Agreement as well as other issues unique to the Texas-Mexico border.
The Texas-Mexico relationship is of "huge" importance to the state, Fero said. Even what constitutes the border area in Texas changes and is open to debate.

"The Texas-Mexico relationship is such a fact of life, and it's going to shape what Texas is over the next generation, and what it becomes," he said. "As one example, a generation from now, there will be no majority ethnic groups in Texas, they will all be minorities. That's one kind of major change."
Fero said while the Anglo population is growing, it is shrinking on a percentage basis. The Hispanic population is growing in both raw numbers and as a percentage of population, he said.
The comptrollers' office began work on the report early this year, and expects to step up its efforts once the Texas legislature ends it session in early June, Fero said.
